name: outcome-mark
purpose: A small round mark that states how something ended: a check for success, a cross for danger, an exclamation for warning and a dash for neutral (not set, not run). It replaces the design sample's `StateMark` and `SuccessMark`. With `animated` the disc scales in and the glyph draws itself when the mark appears and every time its severity changes, so an outcome screen or a finished row can mark the moment a run lands; under reduced motion it shows at once.
useWhen: At the head of an outcome screen (deploy succeeded or failed), at the large size, animated.
In a checklist or a list of steps, at the small size, to say a step is done or not set.
Beside a label that reports a finished run, when the run's state turns from running to an outcome.
avoidWhen: A state that is still running → use `spinner` or `status-indicator` with `loading`.
A labelled status pill in a table cell → use `tag` or `status-indicator`.
A message with text and actions → use `alert` or `toast`.
related: status-indicator` — a coloured dot with a label, for live states.
tag` — a labelled pill for a state.
toast` — reports the outcome of an async action wherever the user is.
bestPractices: Pair the mark with words that say the same thing; the mark is not the only cue.
Animate only the mark that just changed; a list of animated marks on load is noise.
Give a specific `ariaLabel` (`Deployed`, `Done`) when the catalog name is too generic.

props.name: severity
props.doc: The outcome the mark shows: a check, a cross, an exclamation or a dash.

props.name: animated
props.doc: Scales the disc in and draws the glyph when it appears or its severity changes; static under reduced motion.

props.name: ariaLabel
props.doc: Accessible name. Empty uses the locale catalog name of the severity.
